name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,813

entries.clue: Literally resign as number one (6-2-7)

blocks.note: read as quitting a post, and meant as RE-SIGN taken word for word: to sign a second time
read as the boss stepping down, and meant as signing after the boss, who signs first

annotation.surface: A leader quits the top job, word for word.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Literally' tells you to split 'resign' into RE-SIGN. Whoever signs again, after number one, is the deputy.
annotation.definitionFit: A second-in-command is number two, the one whose signature follows number one's.

entries.clue: Sun attempts to keep quiet about beach's standard (5,3,7)

indicatorNotes.to keep: to keep something is to hold it, so TRIES holds P inside it

blocks.note: the sun is a star
a beach's sands
attempts = tries
p = piano, quiet in music

annotation.surface: A tabloid tries to hush up a story about a beach flag.
annotation.walkthrough: A standard here is a flag, not a level of quality. TRIES closes round P to make TRIPES, which ends the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag carried as an emblem, and the Stars and Stripes is the United States flag.

entries.clue: Gas company in charge of heat (7)

blocks.note: Calor Gas, a British supplier of bottled gas
IC = in charge

annotation.surface: A utility firm is responsible for keeping homes warm.
annotation.walkthrough: Calor is a British brand of bottled gas for caravans and heaters, so 'Gas company' is one unit.
annotation.definitionFit: Caloric was the supposed fluid that carried heat in old physics, and the word still names heat.

entries.clue: Born and raised in Greenwich (3)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, lifting letters up makes them read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: grEENwich

annotation.surface: Someone was born and grew up in a London borough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like 'brought up' in the surface but, in a down entry, tells you to read the letters upward.
annotation.definitionFit: Née, from French, means born, used before a woman's maiden name.

entries.clue: Senses petitioner's rant is ill-made (15)

indicatorNotes.ill-made: the letters are badly put together, so rearrange them

blocks.note: the fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: Someone judges a petitioner's tirade to be poorly put together.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, as punctuation usually is. 'Senses' looks like a verb, feels, but is the plural noun: meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: The senses of a word are the meanings it can be given, its possible interpretations.

entries.clue: Guy's stress when Jacob's son acts for new media outlet (5,10)

indicatorNotes.acts for: to act for someone is to stand in for them, so LEVI takes the place of N

blocks.note: a guy is a rope or cable holding something steady
stress = tension
Levi, one of Jacob's twelve sons in Genesis
N = new

annotation.walkthrough: TENSION has its first N swapped for LEVI, making TELEVISION.
annotation.surface: A man is under strain while a Biblical character performs for a fresh channel.
annotation.definitionFit: A media outlet is any channel that carries news or entertainment; cable television is one kind, delivered by wire rather than over the air.

entries.clue: Generous national publication's first intention to embrace love (11)

indicatorNotes.first: take only the opening letter of 'national'
indicatorNotes.to embrace: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so ANIMUS closes its arms round O

blocks.note: a mag is a magazine
its first letter
animus = intention, purpose
love = nil, zero, O in tennis scoring

annotation.surface: A newspaper's leading aim is to be warm-hearted and open.
annotation.walkthrough: ANIMUS usually means hostility, but it also means intention or purpose, which is the sense needed here.
annotation.definitionFit: Magnanimous means generous in spirit, especially towards a rival.

entries.clue: When insurer originally insured weapon (7)

blocks.note: as = when
Saga, a British insurer for the over-fifties
its first letter

annotation.surface: A question about when an insurance company first covered a weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: Saga is a British firm selling insurance and holidays to older people.
annotation.definitionFit: An assagai, also spelt assegai, is a slender spear from southern Africa.

entries.clue: Don's tackling tries in team practices (5,10)

indicatorNotes.tackling: a tackler grabs hold of a player, so REAL takes hold of HEARS by closing round it
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places HEARS inside REAL, where the team is tackling it

blocks.note: to don clothes is to dress
Real Madrid, the football team
a judge tries, or hears, a case
the S of Don's, added at the end

annotation.surface: A university teacher joins the rugby side's training.
annotation.walkthrough: The rugby picture makes 'tries' look like scores, but it is a court verb: a judge hears a case.
annotation.definitionFit: Dress rehearsals are the final practices of a show, done in full costume.

entries.clue: Complaint with food soldiers returned (7)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned is sent back, so LI is set back to front as IL

blocks.note: ALIMENT, food, with the LI in its middle lifted out to be turned
LI = Light Infantry

annotation.surface: Troops send back their meals with a grumble.
annotation.walkthrough: The soldiers are already inside the food: aliment is a formal word for nourishment, and it only needs two letters turning.
annotation.definitionFit: Complaint has a medical sense, a minor illness, which is exactly what an ailment is.

entries.clue: Refuse to get benefit cut (7)

indicatorNotes.cut: chop the last letter off ASSET

blocks.note: to bag = to get
ASSET, a benefit, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone declines to accept a reduced welfare payment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb, but it is the noun: waste.
annotation.definitionFit: Bagasse is the fibrous waste left after sugar cane is crushed.

entries.clue: Tax officer goes round church without leading chaplain (9)

indicatorNotes.goes round: SARGE wraps round the remains of CHURCH
indicatorNotes.without leading: remove CH from the front of CHURCH

blocks.note: sarge, short for sergeant
taken as written
Ch. = chaplain; removed from the front, leaving URCH

annotation.surface: A revenue man makes his rounds of a church whose chaplain has gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax officer' reads as a single job, but the definition is 'Tax' alone and the officer is a sergeant.
annotation.definitionFit: Tax is used loosely for any levy, and a surcharge is an extra levy added on top of a price.

entries.clue: Claret flows from this (11)

blocks.note: read as red Bordeaux wine, and meant as old British boxing slang for blood
read as wine pouring from a bottle, and meant as blood pouring from a wound

annotation.surface: A wine pours from a bottle or cask.
annotation.walkthrough: Claret is red Bordeaux wine, but in old British boxing slang it is blood, so the flow comes from a wound, not a bottle.
annotation.definitionFit: A haemorrhage is heavy bleeding, where blood flows out.

entries.clue: Giant ship docked by you and me (5)

indicatorNotes.docked: cut off the tail, as a dog's tail is docked

blocks.note: ARGO, Jason's ship, without its last letter
you and me = us

annotation.surface: A huge vessel is brought into harbour by the two of us.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Docked' suggests mooring a ship, but it means shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: Argus was the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth.

entries.clue: Might this provide relief from piles?! (7,8)

annotation.definition: Might this provide relief from piles?!

blocks.note: read as a treatment that eases pain, which medicine does
read as haemorrhoids, and meant as atomic piles, the early name for nuclear reactors

annotation.surface: A question about treating haemorrhoids.
annotation.walkthrough: Piles reads as the medical complaint, but an atomic pile is an early nuclear reactor, so the medicine comes from the reactor.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuclear medicine uses radioactive material, made in reactors or piles, to diagnose and treat illness.

entries.clue: It may cause you to swallow your words (4,2,3,6)

annotation.definition: It may cause you to swallow your words

blocks.note: a plain lead-in: the answer is a cause
read as having to retract what you said, and also pictured as the tongue slipping back to gulp them down

annotation.surface: Something that makes you eat your own words.
annotation.walkthrough: Swallowing your words sounds like retracting them, but it also pictures the tongue slipping back down the throat.
annotation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue is a spoken mistake, which you then have to take back.

entries.clue: Island accordingly accommodates motorway in narrow strip of land (7)

indicatorNotes.accommodates: THUS gives room to M inside it

blocks.note: Is. = island
thus = accordingly
M, as in the M1

annotation.surface: An island makes room for a motorway on a thin neck of land.
annotation.walkthrough: British motorways are numbered with M, as in the M1 and M25.
annotation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land joining two larger areas.

entries.clue: Graphical user interface on sailor's instruments (7)

blocks.note: the initials
a tar is a sailor; TAR'S

annotation.surface: A computer screen display running on a ship's navigation equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Instruments' in the surface are navigation dials; the answer is the musical kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Instruments is the category and guitars one member of it: a definition by example, the six-stringed musical kind.

entries.clue: Heard Greek character briefly rushed to make revolutionary device (5)

indicatorNotes.Heard: what the Greek letter's name sounds like
indicatorNotes.briefly: cut the last letter off TORE

blocks.note: rho, the Greek R, said out loud
TORE, rushed, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A Greek is overheard dashing off to build a machine for the rebels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics; here it means something that spins.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, a device that revolves.

entries.clue: Keener row about modern artist (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so TIER sits round HIRST

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
Damien Hirst, the British artist of the shark in formaldehyde

annotation.surface: A more enthusiastic argument about a contemporary painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats. Damien Hirst is the crossword's usual modern artist.
annotation.definitionFit: Thirstier means more eager, as in thirsty for knowledge.

entries.clue: Ritual refusal to swallow a fish (7)

indicatorNotes.to swallow: what you swallow ends up inside you, so POMP NO takes A inside, between its two parts

blocks.note: pomp = ceremonial ritual
taken as written, going between POMP and NO
no = a refusal

annotation.surface: Someone ceremonially declines to eat a fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' sets up a fish being eaten; the only thing swallowed is the letter A.
annotation.definitionFit: The pompano is a food fish of the Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico.

entries.clue: Some like banal form of art (7)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the next words is used

blocks.note: lIKE BANAl

annotation.surface: A critic finds some art dull.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the break between two words, and 'banal' casts art in a dismissive light that hides the Japanese word.
annotation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging.

entries.clue: Mack maybe comes back for fish (3)

indicatorNotes.comes back: coming back is going the way you came, so LEE is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Lee Mack, the British comedian; 'maybe' flags him as one Mack of several

annotation.surface: Someone called Mack returns for his fish supper.
annotation.walkthrough: Lee Mack is a British stand-up and TV comedian, so his surname stands for his first name here.
annotation.definitionFit: An eel is a long, snake-like fish.

entries.clue: Discontented spy stops meeting shrinks and other experts (7,8)

indicatorNotes.Discontented: with its content, the inside, removed, SPY leaves S and Y

blocks.note: the outside letters of SPY
stems = stops, as in stemming a flow
a shrink is a psychiatrist, an analyst

annotation.surface: An unhappy agent stops going to therapists and other specialists.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops' and 'shrinks' both look like verbs in the surface, but 'shrinks' is the noun for therapists. 'Other' marks the answer as experts besides the shrinks.
annotation.definitionFit: Systems analysts are experts who study and design computer systems.
